scope: Follow-up qualification of RUN43 cinnamon research gates: price series, seed-export-ban hypothesis, Kandyan/Asian price knowledge, and cinnamon-to-coffee/tea continuity.

decisions.Q-R43-CINNAMON-SEED-EXPORT-BAN-001: resolved_negative_within_scope; no cinnamon-specific export-ban instrument located, but Hovy/correspondence not exhaustively searched
decisions.Q-R43-CINNAMON-ASIAN-PRICE-KNOWLEDGE-001: open; original falsifier triggered and question split into qualitative Kandyan-value and Asian-merchant-information subquestions
decisions.Q-R43-CINNAMON-TO-COFFEE-TEA-CONTINUITY-: resolved_bounded; spatial discontinuity supported, continuity restricted to export/macro-institutional mechanisms

explicit_exclusions: Do not promote the claim that 2,000 tonnes of cinnamon were burned in Amsterdam in 1760 to raise prices by 400 percent.
Do not promote the claim that one pound of cinnamon equalled one month of a Dutch sailor's wages.
Do not infer a Ceylon cinnamon seed-export prohibition from Moluccan clove/nutmeg extirpation policy.
Do not describe VOC cinnamon gardens as direct cadastral ancestors of British coffee/tea estates.
verification_note: RUN44 independently rechecked the two promoted/refined mechanisms against accessible external sources: Ekama 2022 supports VOC regulation protecting cinnamon-peeler caste duties; Echelon 2018 supports Falck's 1769 seed cultivation and continued compulsory Salagama labour; University of Exeter Taking Tea supports post-1815 Kandyan-highland coffee expansion and coffee infrastructure feeding tea. Direct Hovy, VOC account books and early British land/deed registers remain future archival gates.
